text: Carl Dunmore's own discipline about log backups was the only reason Lesson 1's near-miss didn't cost real data. This video writes down what used to live only in one DBA's head.
Three documents, three jobs: a DR runbook for 2 a.m. under pressure, a security reference for an auditor, and a plain-prose lineage description for anyone, technical or not.
The runbook's key line is a checklist item verifying every connected app resolves through the failover group's listener, not the primary server's own name -- the permanent fix for the drill incident.
A dated DR test log makes failover testing auditable, not anecdotal, and a live thirty-minute walkthrough with the on-call DBA is what keeps the checklist from being skipped under real pressure.
The system can now be run without the person who built it in the room. Last video: the honest wrap-up on what changed and what's still manual.
